bullets.title: SNOW +37% on blockbuster F1Q: AI inflection now fully reflected in guidance
bullets.body: Snowflake delivered 34% product revenue growth (beat of ~5%), raised FY27 product revenue guide to $5.84B (+31% y/y, up 4pts), and guided Q2 at +30% vs. ~26% consensus — all driven by Cortex Code (7,100+ accounts) and Snowflake Intelligence. NRR ticked up for first time in 2+ years to 126%. The company also signed a $6B multi-year AWS infrastructure commitment, its largest ever. PTs across the Street cluster $285-$325 (UBS $325, Wolfe $310, Mizuho $295, Piper $295, KeyBanc $285, GS $278, Citi upgraded to Buy at $260).

bullets.title: MRVL raises FY27/28 outlooks materially; interconnect +70% y/y, custom to $10B by FY29
bullets.body: Marvell guided FY27 revenue to ~$11.5B (+40% y/y) and FY28 to ~$16.5B (+45% y/y), with data center growing +50%/+55% respectively. Interconnect growth raised from +50% to +70% y/y; custom XPU (MSFT Maia 300 ramping, Amazon existing) expected to more than double in FY28 and reach $10B+ in FY29. Optical/CPO to exceed $300M in FY28 (2x prior). Street PTs range $195-$275 (Citi $225, UBS $230, Wolfe $250, ROTH $275, KeyBanc $260, MS raises to $195 but stays Equal-Weight).

bullets.title: CRM in-line quarter; Agentforce ARR crossed $1B but cRPO/bookings disappoint, H2 acceleration uncertain
bullets.body: Salesforce Q1 revenue $11.13B beat by 0.7% with EPS $3.88 (+24%), but cRPO growth at 13% CC was in-line at best, billings missed by 5.7%, and FCF guidance was cut to +4-5% y/y. Agentforce ARR grew 205% y/y to $1.2B (50% q/q), yet only ~3% of total revenue. Management dropped explicit language on 'organic revenue re-acceleration in 2H FY27' from the guidance section. Street broadly holds Neutral to slight positive; Citi maintains Neutral at $187-188, UBS Neutral $185, Wolfe lowers PT to $220, GS lowers to $242.

bullets.title: Geopolitical flare-up: US-Iran strikes resume, crude +3%, S&P futs -0.2%
bullets.body: Fresh US military strikes against Iran in the Strait of Hormuz — the second incident this week — pushed WTI crude up ~3% to ~$90-91/bbl and pulled S&P futures down ~0.2% overnight. Odds of Hormuz reopening by end-June dropped to 35% from 42%. The risk-off move hit airlines and cruises (RCL, CCL -2.6-4.5%), while energy stocks lagged on the paradox of supply disruption vs. demand concerns. 10-year yield +2 bps to 4.51%.

bullets.title: Data center supply chain all-time tight: hyperscaler capex +83% y/y, optical backlog to CY28
bullets.body: GS data center tracker shows project starts +92% y/y and hyperscaler capex +83% y/y, while actual construction is only +34% y/y — a massive execution gap. Geographic bifurcation: Texas +179% y/y vs Virginia +1% y/y. LITE lasers sold out, COHR backlog extends to CY28, MRVL raised interconnect growth to +70% y/y — three layers of the AI optical supply chain all signaling demand outstrips supply. Wiwynn warns of component shortages slowing AI infrastructure development.

bullets.title: SOX +75% YTD — biggest gains since dotcom; semi profit-taking underway but AI theme intact
bullets.body: The FT notes semiconductor stocks are racing toward their largest YTD gains since the dotcom era on AI demand. MRVL +134% YTD, MU +19.3%, SOXX +6.1% YTD. Pre-market sees some profit-taking: INTC -2.3%, ALAB -2.3%, MTSI -2.7%. JPM views semis/AI complex as extended but flags further upside possible with AVGO earnings next week. Mizuho raises MU PT to $1,150 (from $800) and SNDK to $1,825, citing HBM4e pricing up 70-100% y/y and agentic AI driving 9-13% incremental DRAM demand.

bullets.title: META launching subscription tiers; $8B+ medium-term revenue opportunity at 50-70% incremental margins
bullets.body: Meta is rolling out seven subscription tiers across Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp ($2.99-$49.99/month) and testing AI subscriptions at $7.99-$19.99/month. Multiple analysts model ~$8B annualized subscription revenue medium-term with 50-70% incremental OI margins, potentially adding ~$4-5.6B to operating income vs. $90B 2026 estimate. KeyBanc upgrades to Overweight at $760 PT; Mizuho upgrades to Outperform. META CEO also floated cloud computing entry ('MetAWS') if data center overcapacity materializes.

bullets.title: Inflation remains the binding macro constraint; core PCE expected to tick up in April
bullets.body: Multiple strategists flag inflation — not weak demand — as the primary constraint on the economic cycle. US core PCE for April is expected to rise, reinforcing the hawkish Fed shift. The Street consensus S&P year-end target is ~7800. JPM notes a negative correlation between stocks and bond yields reflects inflation as the constraining factor; downside inflation surprises would be 'significantly positive' for risk assets. Fed officials divided: Jefferson expects decline, Cook/Goolsbee warn of persistence.

bullets.title: Broad software rally on SNOW halo: MDB +9.5%, NET +3.3%, NOW +4.8%, TEAM +2.4%
bullets.body: SNOW's blockbuster print is lifting the entire data/infrastructure software complex in pre-market. Analysts explicitly draw read-throughs to consumption-model peers like MDB and ESTC. Karl Keirstead (UBS) reiterates preference for Data/Infra layer over SaaS/Apps. The 'mission-critical vs. replaceable software' separation is widening — SNOW/DDOG-like platforms are favored while application software faces headwinds from AI disruption and muted core growth.

bullets.title: DELL wins $9.7B Pentagon contract; strong AI server demand sets up tonight's earnings
bullets.body: Dell was awarded a $9.7B US military contract for Microsoft software license management, expected to save DoD $422M annually — stock +4.4% pre-market. Citi buyside expectations for tonight's Q are $3.30+ EPS on $40B+ vs. consensus $2.99/$35.5B. Mizuho raises DELL PT to $350.

bullets.title: AI 'tokenmaxxing' backlash emerging: corporate leaders questioning ROI on AI spending
bullets.body: Multiple sources note a growing backlash against 'tokenmaxxing' — the practice of maximizing AI token consumption to justify spending. UBS tech desk flags corporate leaders questioning ROI, while AI capex plans among hyperscalers remain 'set and unlikely to change.' US hyperscalers expected to spend $700B+ on AI infrastructure in 2026 vs. ~$400B in 2025. Amazon reportedly spending $6B to expand agentic capabilities, supporting the data/infrastructure layer over weaker application software names.

bullets.title: Equity market structure: SPX at ATH, dealers long gamma, single-stock vols at 95th pctile
bullets.body: S&P and Nasdaq closed at all-time highs. Citi notes S&P 500 average earnings-day returns of +67bps — highest since 2019 — and upside vol 30% higher than downside, a 14-year high. Dealers are meaningfully long SPX gamma, dampening index vol. Single-stock 3M implied vol at 95th percentile; put-call skew at 1Y lows indicating bullish positioning. After 5 straight up days, Hedgeye flags short-term overbought conditions. VIX risk range 15.79-18.14.

bullets.title: Week ahead: ISM Mfg Jun 1, NFP Jun 5, AVGO earnings Jun 3 — all potential tape-movers
bullets.body: JPM macro calendar for week of June 1 includes ISM Manufacturing (Jun 1), ADP (Jun 4), NFP (Jun 5), Fed Beige Book (Jun 3), and AVGO earnings (Jun 3, consensus EPS $2.39 on $22.04B revenue). AVGO is the most anticipated semi catalyst after MRVL's strong print. G7 Summit Jun 15-17. USMCA joint review mandatory Jul 1; trade truce agreement expires Nov 1.

bullets.title: Agentic CPU: AMD biggest winner, NVDA modest EPS uplift, INTC faces share loss to Axion
bullets.body: Wolfe models ~30% CPU TAM growth through CY28 from agentic+orchestration workloads. AMD server CPU revenue could reach $44B by CY28 (vs $17B CY26), adding $7 incremental EPS. NVDA ships >4M CPUs this year (1.3M Vera in Q4) for $6.6B incremental revenue but only ~$0.50 EPS uplift on large base. INTC modeled at $1 incremental EPS but faces share loss as Google moves to Axion. ARM expected $1.25 EPS uplift from datacenter royalties, growing to ~45% of total CPU by CY28 from 15% today.

bullets.title: TSMC raising 3nm pricing 15% in 2H26; Fab 18 queue shows no sign of easing
bullets.body: Korean sources report TSMC is raising 3nm pricing up to 15% in 2H26, with a further 5-10% hike in 2027. Monthly 3nm capacity rose from 130K to 160-175K wafers in Q2, but customer queues at Fab 18 show little relief. US hyperscalers expected to spend $700B+ on AI infrastructure in 2026 vs. ~$400B in 2025. Tight TSMC capacity through CY28 is expected to drive agentic CPU market share more than performance.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler macro: strong labor data and tax cuts support 3% real consumer spending despite energy shock
bullets.body: Piper Sandler notes household spending plans hit a 3-year high on record employment and declining unemployment claims. The $180B individual tax cut, lower tariffs, and easier lending standards support consumer spending. The energy shock is described as less than one-quarter the size of income growth plus tax relief in aggregate. JPM and BofA separately report consumer remains healthy with MTD spending up ~5%.

bullets.title: NVDA teases surprise new product; testing GPU-to-GPU hybrid bonding (N1/N1X candidate)
bullets.body: Jensen Huang publicly stated Nvidia has 'a surprising new product that we haven't told anyone about.' Separately, sell-side research indicates NVIDIA is testing GPU-to-GPU hybrid bonding with N1/N1X as the most likely candidate. Intel is investing several billion dollars in EMIB packaging as a cost-competitive alternative to TSMC's 2.5D silicon interposer approach.

bullets.title: UBER raises Delivery Hero stake to ~37%; acquisition intent viewed as probable
bullets.body: Uber increased its stake in Delivery Hero from ~25% to ~36.8% via €40/share Aspex acquisition, with voting rights capped at 24.99% to block rival bids. JPM's Schilsky views acquisition intent as probable. UBER also raised stake in DHER.GY disclosed in overnight notes.

bullets.title: EM AI hardware trade: JPM raises MXEF target to 2000; Korea +203% EPS y/y, Taiwan +49%
bullets.body: JPM raises MXEF base/bull/bear targets to 2000/2200/1500 on AI hardware concentration. MSCI EM consensus 2026 EPS revised up +55%, driven by Korea (+203% y/y) and Taiwan (+49% y/y). SK Hynix struck a 'longer and higher' memory cycle tone with HBM demand to exceed supply for the next three years. China AI profit pool is expanding but economic surplus is accruing upstream to compute owners, not model-layer companies.

bullets.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: FOXA, CMCSA/Telemundo, TKO, ROKU key beneficiaries; $850M+ ad revenue
bullets.body: MS models $300-400M in World Cup advertising revenue for Fox Sports (FOXA) with upside to $500M+; Sportico projects $850M combined for Fox Sports and Telemundo (CMCSA). TKO's OnLocation premium hospitality could see a +$75M EBITDA tailwind. ROKU benefits from Fox One FAST channel launch at $19.99/month. MS Economics forecasts a +10-15bps boost to US consumption in June/July and +20K potential boost to June payrolls.
